title: Building Reliable Data Analytics Agents: Lessons from the KDD Cup | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA's KGMON team placed second in the KDD Cup 2026 Data Agents competition using a small fixed LLM, arguing that agent reliability comes mainly from a constrained harness: unified SQLite query surface, schema preflight, a tiny opinionated toolset, isolated prose extraction, and trace-based failure inspection. They caution that ensembling and autonomous improvement loops raise cost and overfitting risk.

insights.claim: NVIDIA's KGMON team placed second in the KDD Cup 2026 Data Agents competition with a system built around making the agent harness smaller, clearer and easier to verify.
insights.speaker: Eduardo Rocha de Andrade
insights.so_what: Competitive results show harness engineering can substitute for larger models.

insights.claim: Because KDD required a small fixed LLM, the harness became the main optimization surface, and these techniques are especially useful for reliable systems around smaller open models.
insights.speaker: Eduardo Rocha de Andrade
insights.so_what: Value in agentic AI may accrue to orchestration/tooling layers, enabling cheaper small open models.
insights.quote: KDD also required teams to work with a small, fixed LLM to power the agent, making the harness the main optimization surface.

insights.claim: Agent reliability often comes less from making the model more open-ended and more from building the right harness around it.
insights.speaker: Eduardo Rocha de Andrade
insights.so_what: Counters the 'bigger model solves it' narrative; supports agent-infrastructure investment theses.
insights.quote: Reliability often comes less from making the model more open-ended and more from building the right harness around it.

insights.claim: Two principles drove the design: constrain the action space and make every attempt inspectable.
insights.speaker: Eduardo Rocha de Andrade
insights.so_what: Concise design framework for evaluating enterprise agent products.

insights.claim: KGMON converted CSV and JSON files into tables in a single SQLite database exposed via schema() and sql(query), which reduced routing failures and wasted turns and left the fixed model more room to reason.
insights.speaker: Eduardo Rocha de Andrade
insights.so_what: Data normalization layers (warehouses, virtualized query engines) are key enablers for analytics agents.
insights.quote: The single SQL interface reduced routing failures and wasted turns, leaving the fixed model more room to reason over the data.

insights.claim: A read-only schema-scouting preflight that briefs the agent on tables, join keys, units, null patterns and look-alike fields reduced errors from wrong columns and missed joins, and can be more useful than another retrieval tool.
insights.speaker: Eduardo Rocha de Andrade
insights.so_what: Metadata/catalog quality may matter more for agent accuracy than retrieval tooling.
insights.quote: This can be more useful than another retrieval tool.

insights.claim: The agent was limited to a small toolset (schema, sql, write_answer, prose_helper), with middleware repairing malformed tool calls and a persistent Python state retaining intermediate results.
insights.speaker: Eduardo Rocha de Andrade
insights.so_what: Small, opinionated tool surfaces are a design pattern for reliable enterprise agents.

insights.claim: Short, valid attempts freed turns for additional runs, evaluation and ensembling.
insights.speaker: Eduardo Rocha de Andrade
insights.so_what: Efficiency per attempt compounds into accuracy via ensembling within budget.
insights.quote: Short, valid attempts left more turns for additional runs, evaluation, and ensembling

insights.claim: KGMON blocked full-file reads and used a prose_helper tool that sent document chunks to a separate zero-temperature LLM call with reasoning disabled, returning answers or extracted tables while keeping raw prose out of the main agent's context.
insights.speaker: Eduardo Rocha de Andrade
insights.so_what: Context-window management via sub-calls is a core cost/accuracy lever for agents.

insights.claim: To avoid compute cost of video in the agent loop, KGMON preprocessed briefing videos by extracting keyframes, transcribing audio and aligning transcripts with frames, since videos often contained slide-based constraints or distractor values.
insights.speaker: Eduardo Rocha de Andrade
insights.so_what: Multimodal preprocessing pipelines are part of practical agent stacks.

insights.claim: Each attempt logged prompts, tool calls, SQL, intermediate results and errors, enabling a specialized inspector agent to categorize failures and prioritize harness improvements.
insights.speaker: Eduardo Rocha de Andrade
insights.so_what: Observability/tracing is a growth area for agent tooling vendors.

insights.claim: Repeated attempts grouped by answer values improved coverage, but ensembling increases token usage, latency and compute cost, so in production it should be reserved for high-value or uncertain tasks.
insights.speaker: Eduardo Rocha de Andrade
insights.so_what: Ensembling drives inference token demand; selective use limits cost but raises compute consumption overall.
insights.quote: Repeated attempts increase token usage, latency, and compute cost.

insights.claim: Autonomous improvement loops risk overfitting through hardcoded training examples, contradictory instructions, brittle postprocessing and gains on one benchmark split that hurt generalization.
insights.speaker: Eduardo Rocha de Andrade
insights.so_what: Benchmark scores of self-improving agents may overstate real-world performance.

insights.claim: Humans should define tasks, audit traces and approve which improvements to retain, while agents execute and explore, rather than overseeing every tool call.
insights.speaker: Eduardo Rocha de Andrade
insights.so_what: Human-in-the-loop governance remains central to deploying enterprise agents.
insights.quote: Let agents execute and explore, while people decide which improvements to retain.
